graders.run: uv run pytest .flywheel/holdout/00032-postgres-read-path-parity -k "postgres and not refus"
graders.name: seam-returns-usable-postgres-holdout

goal: Lift the Postgres refusal in the read-verb store-construction seam so a successfully constructed PostgresStore is returned un-closed to the caller, while the no-DSN and missing-extra fail-fast paths still exit non-zero with their actionable messages.

relevant: packages/flywheel-orchestrator/src/flywheel_orchestrator/_store_factory.py:142-168 -- open_sqlite_bound_store builds the store then closes-and-raises StoreConfigError for a PostgresStore; lift ONLY that constructed-postgres-store-refuse branch so the store is returned to the caller

packages/flywheel-orchestrator/tests/test_store_factory.py:228 -- test_open_sqlite_bound_store_refuses_postgres asserts the refusal this task removes; replace it with an equal-or-greater assertion that the seam returns a usable (un-closed) PostgresStore for a postgres policy with the container reachable
packages/flywheel-orchestrator/tests/test_store_factory.py:118-167 -- the no-DSN (without_env_vars) and missing-extra fail-fast tests that must stay green unchanged
references: .flywheel/holdout/00032-postgres-read-path-parity/ -- the held-out grader sets FLYWHEEL_PG_DSN, calls the seam with a postgres policy, and uses the returned store for a read (so a closed store fails it)
packages/flywheel-orchestrator/src/flywheel_orchestrator/_orchestrate.py:521 -- consumer that calls open_sqlite_bound_store for the orchestrate control-store reads
packages/flywheel/src/flywheel/_tui.py:312 -- consumer that calls open_sqlite_bound_store for status/live/history/show
constraints: Preserve the fail-fast paths VERBATIM (spec D-4): a postgres backend with neither FLYWHEEL_PG_DSN nor DATABASE_URL set still raises StoreConfigError naming both env vars and exits non-zero; the missing-extra case still names the install command. Only the constructed-postgres-store -> refuse branch is removed.

When the refusal assertion is removed, a replacement assertion of equal-or-greater strength covering the accept-and-return behavior must exist in the same test file (criterion 9): assert open_sqlite_bound_store (or its successor) returns a usable PostgresStore for a postgres policy with the container reachable, and that the old test no longer asserts a StoreConfigError is raised for a reachable Postgres store.
The returned store must be un-closed and usable for a read; do not return a closed store.
Commit the change with a clear message before reporting done.
non_goals: Do not modify, read, or author anything under .flywheel/holdout/00032-postgres-read-path-parity/.

Do not weaken or delete the no-DSN / missing-extra fail-fast tests, nor any other assertion in test_store_factory.py beyond replacing the single refusal assertion with an equal-or-greater accept-and-return one.
Do not touch the read-path port functions or the query-surface protocol (owned by pg-read-path-port and 00030/00031).
Do not change DSN resolution, the init/config write path, or the missing-extra error text.
edge_cases: Keeping the refusal but only widening its message must fail the seam-returns-usable-postgres holdout (the store must actually be returned and usable).
Returning a closed store must fail the holdout (it uses the returned store for a read).
Collapsing the no-DSN path into the now-accepted construction path (silent build or sqlite fallback) must fail no-dsn-fail-fast-preserved, which asserts the named-both-vars message and non-zero exit.
notes: Renaming the now-misnamed open_sqlite_bound_store seam is a path-level decision left to the implementer (spec D-4); not graded. Update every call site (orchestrate.py, _tui.py) in the same change if renamed.
This task depends on pg-read-path-port because the reads must already route through the backend-agnostic surface before the refusal can be safely lifted.
